Rather than retaining fragmented point-to-point integrations, the gateway connected ACCESS to clearing networks and internal compliance, settlement, and reporting systems.

For administrators, Matt replaced individual permission configuration with role-based profiles and bulk changes across users, accounts, and products. Entitlement management dropped from **days to minutes**. For regional compliance teams, he translated jurisdiction-specific requirements into data visibility and access controls, sequencing launches by regulatory readiness rather than a single global deployment.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**. The payments migration completed **without disruption to live payment operations**, preserving client configurations, entitlements, transaction histories, and compliance traceability. Matt also owned production incident response, coordinating root-cause analysis and leadership updates when payment issues surfaced.

🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. He describes many teams he inherited as “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His focus is on removing those barriers: making intent explicit, building psychological safety so people can speak honestly, and pushing decisions to the people closest to the work.

At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, he established a “permit to fail” learning environment. Teams had avoided risks because they feared blame, slowing experimentation and delivery. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems and supported lean, low-stakes experiments with structured hypotheses and controlled iterations. Instead of pointing fingers, teams applied lessons from mistakes to subsequent sprints.

In innovation work, he set expectations that early prototypes and user tests would likely fail, intentionally. He used user research, Jobs to Be Done framing, and rapid testing to challenge assumptions before committing to costly builds. Failed experiments became decision inputs rather than setbacks.

He also built balanced teams: Product + Engineering + Design together, with equal participation and shared accountability. Engineers, product managers, and UX architects worked together rather than handing work across role silos. Pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, automation, and continuous delivery were part of daily work.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams achieved **4x delivery acceleration** after embracing lean product and modern engineering practices. His balanced-team work also achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.

The Cloud Innovation Centers delivered **30+ product engagements** across **15+ Fortune 500 clients**, achieving **4X faster velocity** and **zero-defect deployments**. answer_md:
🐾 Here’s a time Matt failed.

Matt was the tech lead on a global platform modernization delivery for a **Fortune 500 financial services client**. The program was under delivery pressure, with offshore teams executing test cycles across development, QA, UAT, and production environments. IAM controls, environment segregation, and downstream access configurations had been inherited from prior phases.

Matt was responsible for ensuring a safe environment setup, but he relied on assumptions rather than verifying those controls. He focused on delivery pressures, trusted inherited documentation without confirming its accuracy, and did not audit who could trigger downstream jobs or email processes. He also did not verify whether production customer names and email addresses had been masked or scrubbed in downstream environments. Data masking and email interception were not in place as compensating controls.

An offshore tester accidentally triggered an email job in UAT. It sent communications containing unmasked production customer data to **thousands of real clients**.

Matt took accountability and led the team through root cause analysis and remediation. They identified insufficient IAM checks, unclear environment boundaries, and production data that had not been scrubbed, then worked collectively to implement corrective controls. The client nevertheless demanded that the tester be removed from the project. Matt described that as “a systemic failure that resulted in an individual consequence.”

Afterward, Matt made IAM validation, environment verification, PII scrubbing, and risk ownership day-one responsibilities in his delivery approach. His stated lesson was that “assumptions are risks in disguise.”

At **Accenture’s** Liquid Studio, traditional training programs couldn’t keep pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The AWS Launchpad program was developed in partnership with AWS to address those gaps through tailored enablement rather than theory alone.

Matt led Launchpad at the Atlanta Innovation Hub from **July 2018** to **November 2019**. His task was to build deep cloud competencies across **Accenture**, certify engineers, and prepare teams to lead cloud-native transformation initiatives.

He designed structured learning paths and certification programs covering AWS core services, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, and ECS/Fargate, alongside cloud-native application development. The curriculum combined certification preparation with interactive workshops and hands-on labs, immersing engineers in real-world AWS environments to reinforce practical application over theory.

Matt also established cloud expert mentorship teams so engineers could learn AWS best practices from experienced practitioners. He organized group coaching sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops, making mentorship and peer learning part of the program rather than leaving participants to work through certification material independently. Those practices supported ongoing competency growth beyond the initial training.

Through Launchpad, **more than 200 professionals earned AWS certifications**, including AWS Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption and the launch of cloud-native initiatives at **Accenture**, with structured learning paths, practical labs, and expert mentorship supporting engineers as they prepared for cloud transformation projects.
